newsitem.title: USA: Southern states interest in Berlin utility.
newsitem.headline: Southern states interest in Berlin utility.

text.p: Southern Co said on Tuesday that it has submitted a statement of interest in the stake in German utility Bewag currently held by the government entity, Land Berlin.

"Yesterday, Southern Energy Inc, which is our international unit, submitted a letter of proposal to Land Berlin related to the purchase of this stake in Bewag," said Southern Co spokesman David Mould.
"This is not an actual bid. This is a preliminary step toward that...we would hope to be selected by Land Berlin to then negotiate the purchase of an interest," he said.
Mould could not say whether the Southern Co proposal contained a dollar figure or specified the size of the stake the company would be interested in acquiring.

Published reports have said the sale of the city of Berlin's 50.8 percent stake in Bewag through Land Berlin could raise $2 billion. But left-wing groups in the city's ruling Social Democratic Party have been fighting to limit the offered stake to 25.8 percent.
If Southern Co was to acquire a stake, Mould said the transaction would give the utility its first presence in Continental Europe. It has utility properties in Britain.
The Southern Co spokesman later said he had confirmed with executives in Germany that the utility's proposal contained a monetary figure.

"We are indeed characterizing this as a bid. It's preliminary but definitely a bid ... there is a price," Mould said. "The government (now) will consider the proposals it received and get back to whoever is selected to negotiate."
